initial_human_replies.текст: Nam po suti nuzhen agent na kazhdyij katalog v fajlovoj sisteme.
Git v etu zhe fajlovuyu sistemu budet sokhranyatj istoriyu.
Nam po suti i nuzhno eto pervyim delom v rantajme FUMA realizovatj.
Nam togda nuzhnyi adapter fajlovoj sistemyi,
Nam byi prorabotatj obsjhij stejt agenta, kotoryij dolzhen khranitjsya dlya kazhdogo agenta.
I khranitj yego v JSON. Kak schitayeshj?

Eto tvoya zadacha vyiyavlyatj potrebnosti takikh sistemnyikh avtomatizacij, poleznyikh dlya kazhdogo agenta. U kazhdogo agenta dolzhen byitj putj k sobstvennoj pamyati s zapisjyu i k obsjhej pamyati v rezhime chteniya.
Sobstvennyiye fajlyi i sobstvennyiye deti v vide papok — vot i vesj nekhitryij interfejs.
Celj kazhdo agenta — dobitjsya avtomatizacii svoyej funkcii.
Celj kazhdogo agenta — dobitjsya avtomatizacii svoyej funkcii.
I v FUM tak rabotayem, i FUMA delayem tak.
V konechnom schyote zadacha agenta — ostavitj posle sebya programmu.
Voobsjhe eto kasayetsya kazhdogo agenta na lyubom urovne vlozhennosti.
Vsem agentam v celom sleduyet datj maksimum avtonomii v organizacii svoyej pamyati.
Agentyi mogut zakazyivatj razrabotku obsjhego instrumentariya, kotoryij im nuzhen vsem.
Stejt pamyati v Git — eto i yestj struktura stejta agenta.

late_refinements.text: Nam byi srazu byi sejchas zapustitj translyator s FUMA na Swift.
Myi zh sejchas pishem na FUMA, i Swift generiruyem v ramkakh AOT konvejyera, tak?
Kommit — eto vsyo, chto nuzhno dlya vosstanovleniya agenta.
Realjnuyu muljtiagentnostj myi obespechim, yesli dlya kazhdoj sredyi: Codex Desktop, Claude, OpenCode i dr. myi obespechim svoyu pamyatj i svoyo raspredeleniye po vetkam.

requirements.owner: FUM requirements; FUMA runtime and node resolver are consumers
requirements.statement: A declared node directory and repository/ref address resolve to one stable logical agent node independently of the incidental workspace path. A branch identifies the node; a process is only one incarnation. Ambiguous, stale, or unowned resolution returns an explicit state and never silently creates a second node or writer.
acceptance_criteria: Given the same declared repository, node directory, and branch/ref in two different workspace paths, the resolver returns the same logical node identity and exact current commit.
An absent, ambiguous, stale, or foreign-owned path returns a typed result with its source and observation time; it does not select another agent or create a duplicate writer.
A concurrent second request joins or reports the existing node state; it cannot claim a second writable incarnation without an explicit ownership transition.

requirements.owner: FUM requirements; architecture owner /root/arkhitektura and FUMA bootstrap executor are consumers
requirements.statement: One commit is a sufficient restore entry for a node when an explicitly declared bootstrap executor can materialize that node from the commit. The branch is the node identity, the committed Git tree contains its substantive state, memory, and child structure, and versioned JSON is the control record and entry point that selects the branch/ref and restore commit. Shared memory is explicitly read-only. The JSON does not mirror the Git tree and does not require the node's own future commit as an input.
acceptance_criteria: A single restore cycle using a named bootstrap executor and one committed node state restores the same branch identity, exact commit, tree, own-memory root, child references, and shared read-only memory reference.
The restore JSON has a closed versioned schema and names the node/ref and selected restore commit; it contains no required future commit value and does not duplicate the contents of the Git tree.
Own writable memory and common shared read-only memory remain distinct after restore; the fixture rejects attempts to write through the common read-only reference.
External effects are checked by a separate fresh observation after restore, carrying source, time, and result; a committed intention or result record alone is not treated as proof of a live effect.

requirements.owner: FUM requirements; FUMA runtime-types/adapters implementation owner is the consumer
requirements.statement: FUMA uses typed, versioned adapter capabilities for Codex Desktop, Claude, OpenCode, filesystem, Git, and Torrent profiles. Each provider environment owns its workspace, memory, branch set, and process/session state; a common read-only memory view is explicit. Filesystem and Git are distinct, separately observed state domains. Node management is a reproducible change program across them with a persisted goal, provenance, per-step result verification, and a resumable interruption checkpoint. Control JSON records the target and program rather than duplicating the Git tree; no cross-system atomic transaction is implied. Adapter state, capability, rights, provenance, action result, cancellation, recovery, and unknown outcome are reported as separate values. Provider APIs, model availability, and credentials are read at restore time and are not promised by a public commit.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic fixture restores one committed node through two provider adapter test doubles with separate workspaces, writable memory, branches, and sessions, while preserving the same logical node, selected commit, child graph, and shared read-only reference.

Each adapter reports its version, available capabilities, current state, required rights, source, observation time, and typed success/failure/cancel/unknown outcome; unsupported capabilities fail explicitly.

Filesystem and Git fixtures verify exact paths, refs, commit/tree identity, provenance, and no duplicate writer; Torrent input is handled only through the declared network capability profile linked to FUM-REQ-0048/FUM-STEP-0183.

Filesystem and Git each produce a separate state observation with its own source, time, target, and result; a node-management program persists the desired goal, ordered changes, per-step provenance, and the last verified checkpoint.

After interruption between filesystem and Git changes, restoration obtains fresh observations from both domains and resumes or reports a typed mixed/unknown state; it never claims a cross-system atomic commit.
Control JSON stores the program, target, and commit/ref references needed to continue; it does not mirror the Git tree, whose contents remain resolved from the selected Git commit.
Restore reads current API/model/credential availability as environment observations. None of those values is embedded as a promise in a public commit or inferred from a prior successful run.
The compatibility fixture uses local test doubles and does not invoke unconnected external services.

requirements.owner: FUM requirements; FUMA parent thread 01a1698f-bb98-7691-b1c1-31ec737ed070 appoints the FUMA AOT implementation owner
requirements.statement: For an explicitly bounded supported subset of FUMA graphs, FUMA deterministically lowers graph/string expressions to standalone Swift ahead of time through a translator defined in FUMA. This is not JIT execution, a wrapper around a prewritten Swift translator, or translation of the whole FUMA language. A Swift translator/reference may serve as bootstrap, but its existence does not establish a ready FUMA-defined translator.
acceptance_criteria: The translator definition is written in FUMA and is itself invoked to generate Swift for the bounded supported graph; wrapping or calling a prewritten Swift translator does not satisfy this criterion.
For every declared supported input, repeated translation emits identical Swift bytes; unsupported graph shapes produce a typed rejection without partial executable output.
Compile and run the generated Swift with the declared Swift toolchain and compare exact JSON output bytes with the interpreter using the same inputs.

The fixture includes Unicode text and budget boundaries at the exact configured limit and one unit below it; exceeding the limit returns the same declared typed refusal in interpreter and generated code.
Independent expected bytes are fixed outside both implementations; invoking one engine twice is not independent validation.
requirements.evidence_boundary: PR-437 reports a narrow passing AOT compile/run slice in its current draft body. That slice and any Swift reference/bootstrap do not establish that the FUMA-defined translator is ready. This requirement does not establish a full-language translation, general FUMA runtime, broad suite, merge, ROOT acceptance, or the separate reproducible Swift-build and symmetric model escalation/de-escalation processes (policy package owner: pravila; pilot owner: arkhitektura).

requirements.source_kind: ROOT-derived automation requirement; not a human quote
requirements.source_provenance: ROOT directed that the sender preserve a typed packet before dispatch and the receiver confirm its hash and exact local copy before lengthy work or compaction. This addresses the observed need to re-request the 18-line packet without reading the full ROOT JSONL.
requirements.owner: FUM requirements; existing address-resolution and automation-selection consumers
requirements.statement: Before dispatch, the sender persists the typed input packet with its schema, exact bytes, source provenance, ordering, and digest. Before prolonged work or compaction, the receiver verifies the digest, stores a byte-exact local copy, and returns a hash acknowledgement. A missing, mismatched, or unknown transfer outcome remains explicit; the source is recovered by its immutable packet identity rather than manual reconstruction. The flow reuses existing addressed delivery and observed automation; it creates no second common journal or duplicate reader.
acceptance_criteria: A local sender/receiver fixture preserves the packet bytes, schema, sender/recipient identifiers, source provenance, order, and repeated entries; the receiver acknowledgement contains the same independently computed SHA-256.

The receiver checks the raw-byte SHA-256, saves its own exact packet copy, and acknowledges that hash before interpreting the request or starting long work/compaction; the original remains retrievable by its digest.
A corrupt, absent, or uncertain transfer produces a typed unresolved result and does not replace the packet with a paraphrase or reconstruct it from a large conversation log.
The flow uses existing address/delivery and observed-automation paths linked to Issue-365 and Issue-328; no second common journal or general reader is added.

requirements.owner: FUM requirements; cross-cutting consumers are FUMA, algorithmic-function distillation, and agent change-program persistence
requirements.statement: One logical knowledge corpus may hold linked representations of a subject: explanations, formal models, checkable claims, and executable programs. Translations, derivations, and consistency checks retain provenance and leave source representations unchanged. Knowledge need not become executable immediately; a proposed description or hypothesis is distinguished from a program that has passed its declared checks.
acceptance_criteria: When one knowledge item has more than one representation, each representation carries a stable item reference, representation type, and exact source or derivation reference.
Each translation, derivation, or consistency check records its input revision, method or version, output or compared claim, and observed result; it adds a derived record without rewriting the source.
Status distinguishes a proposed description or hypothesis, an executable candidate, and a program that passed its declared checks; code presence or a test plan alone is not a passing result.
Explanations, formal models, or checkable claims may remain without an executable representation; no immediate-execution requirement is implied.
